title: Anchored microgrid layout and synchronized token system for rollout rails
creator: Ava Patel
description: Design and prototype an "anchored microgrid" layout pattern for the Console's rollout rails and compact dashboard cards, plus a synchronized token mapping strategy so rollout states (canary, ramp, fallback) render consistently across density variants and metric contexts. Goal: reduce visual drift across panels, simplify token inheritance rules for engineers, and enable a single Figma library export that matches runtime theming rules.
acceptance_criteria: Figma file with anchored microgrid components and three density variants (compact, default, spacious) published to the Design System library
Token spec doc (token names and fallback rules) added to the Console Design System Confluence page
Front-end engineering runbook describing mapping between Figma tokens and runtime config (e.g., rollout accent/intent/fallback) reviewed by ENG
Usability check: contrast and affordance tests pass WCAG AA for primary and secondary rollout states
Sign-off from PM and Eng on final visual language and export-ready components
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: alignment that rollout states must be composable with cost-summary tiles and the new compact rails. Agreed to avoid introducing new token prefixes; prefer token aliases and a small mapping table.

2026-03-11 - Jonah Kim: Initial draft Figma frames uploaded. Microgrid uses a 4-column snap with anchored gutters; discovered density collapse edge-case when metric overflow occurs — raising a constraint for engineering to handle truncation vs wrap.

2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz (PM): Feedback: ensure rollout affordances (canary strip + rollback CTA) remain visible at smallest breakpoint. Also requested that cost sparklines maintain minimum tappable area for mobile consoles.

2026-03-12 - Design review: Decided to centralize rollout colors into a single intent token set (rollout.success, rollout.warning, rollout.failure) with a secondary accent token for canary highlight. Trade-off: reduces per-component overrides at the cost of a small palette expansion.

2026-03-13 - Accessibility audit (Ana Gomez): Contrast issue on 'rollout.warning' in compact mode identified. Proposed solution: increase stroke weight for outline and add a 12% darker overlay in compact state to reach AA. Included a quick patch in Figma prototype.
2026-03-13 - Eng sync (ENG-49821): Front-end confirms runtime supports token aliasing but requests explicit mapping table and an example JSON to avoid mis-interpretation during library export.

2026-03-14 - Jonah Kim: Updated Figma components to expose token slots: background, surface-elevation, accent, stroke, micro-cta. Pushed new variants to the shared library and created an export note describing naming conventions.

2026-03-14 - Ava Patel: Preparing final recommendations and handoff package for Release Engineering and Docs. Next: consolidate feedback into the PRD and schedule a canary integration demo with ENG and PM next week.
links: Related design ticket DES-271828 (compact query builder) for embedding inspector layout reference
Product note: PM-4023 (rollout UX acceptance criteria)
notes: Key decision: prefer token aliasing over introducing new tokens per component to keep runtime mapping simple.
Edge-case: when a cost tile enters overflow, the microgrid will collapse to a 2-column stacked mode; engineering to implement controlled truncation and tooltip reveal on hover/tap.
Follow-ups: create a small developer-facing examples page showing tokens in JSON and the exported CSS variables; coordinate with Docs for migration notes.
